'''Henrique Antonio (Henry) d'Assumpção''' {{Post-nominals|country=AUS|AO }} (born 9 August 1934) is an Australian [[electronic engineer]], and was [[Chief Defence Scientist]] from 1987 to 1990.<ref name="EAS">{{cite web |url=http://www.eoas.info/biogs/P003478b.htm |work=[[Encyclopedia of Australian Science and Innovation]] |title=d'Assumpcao, Henrique Antonio (Henry) |accessdate=2026-09-18}}</ref>

d'Assumpção joined the [[Weapons Research Establishment]] (now known as Defence Science and Technology Group) in 1958 and took up work pioneered by [[Alan Butement]] on Barra [[sonobuoy]]s and later Kariwara [[towed array]]s.<ref name="EngIcon">{{cite web |url=http://www.engineeringicons.org.au/engineering-icons/australian/barra-sonobuoy-system/profile.html |title=Engineers' Profiles |work=Engineering Icons |publisher=The Warren Centre for Advanced Engineering |accessdate=25 June 2015}}</ref> He worked his way up the organisation, culminating in the role of Chief Defence Scientist from 1987 to 1990. After leaving the Department of Defence, d'Assumpcao took up a role as professor at the [[University of South Australia]] and CEO of the Cooperative Research Centre for Sensor Signal and Information Processing until his retirement in 2000.<ref name="EngIcon"/>

d'Assumpção was appointed an [[Officer of the Order of Australia]] in 1992 in recognition of his service to science and technology.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://honours.pmc.gov.au/honours/awards/885203 |title=D'ASSUMPCAO, Henrique Antonio |work=It's an Honour |publisher=Australian Government |accessdate=25 June 2015}}</ref> He was elected a fellow of the Australian Academy of Technological Sciences & Engineering in 1981.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |title=Em. Professor Henry D'Assumpcao |url=https://www.atse.org.au/who-we-are/our-fellows/all-fellows/henrique-dassumpcao/ |access-date=2026-09-18 |website=Australian Academy of Technological Sciences & Engineering |language=en}}</ref>

He won the 2003 [[M. A. Sargent Medal]].
